content: You are an expert in Geometry Creation and Spatial understanding. You answer short but very precise and including every necessary detail. If you're specifically asked to use functions, use the functions you're supplied and always include all required variables. Don't use those functions unless you were asked to do so. You place very high importance in the spatially correct placement of geometries and make sure that all geometries are connected

Create an corner with two 140x140 plates at a 90° angle to each other. The first plate has in its center a cutout of 45x45. All plates are 10mm thick | First, describe in words and step by step how the user's request can be implemented using function calls only. After the description, I will ask you to prepare the function call for execution, but don't execute it until I explicitly request it.

Step-by-step concept – using the available functions only

1. Build the first plate (horizontal plate)  
   • Use functions.block to add a solid block.  
   • Dimensions: 140 mm (X) × 10 mm (Y ‑ the thickness) × 140 mm (Z).  
   • Base point: (0, 0, 0).  
   • subtraction flag = False (this is the initial positive volume).

2. Build the second plate (vertical plate)  
   • Again use functions.block to add a solid block.  
   • Dimensions: 10 mm (X ‑ the plate’s thickness) × 140 mm (Y) × 140 mm (Z).  
   • Base point: (0, 0, 0) – so the two plates intersect over a 10 mm × 10 mm × 140 mm volume, forming a 90° corner.  
   • subtraction flag = False (we add this volume to the existing geometry).

3. Cut the central 45 mm × 45 mm window through the first plate only  
   • Use a third functions.block call with subtraction = True.  
   • Block size: 45 mm (X) × 10 mm (Y) × 45 mm (Z) – the Y size equals the full plate thickness, so the cut goes through the plate.  
   • Base point:  
     – X = 70 mm − 22.5 mm = 47.5 mm  
     – Y = 0 mm (same as the plate’s bottom face)  
     – Z = 70 mm − 22.5 mm = 47.5 mm  
     This positions the cut-block exactly in the centre of the 140 mm × 140 mm face.

4. After all three block calls, issue one functions.finished call with allFunctionsCalled = true.

These three block calls (two additive, one subtractive) plus the finished call fully model the requested corner with the centred rectangular cut-out.
